questions.question: What is the 6-gate AI feature decision framework?
options: A model evaluation pipeline with 6 metrics
A structured checklist evaluating problem fit, data, privacy, failure severity, alternatives, and success metrics before building an AI feature
A 6-layer neural network architecture
A deployment pipeline with 6 stages
questions.explanation: The 6-gate framework evaluates: (1) Is this a real problem? (2) Do we have the data? (3) What are the privacy implications? (4) How severe are failures? (5) Are there simpler alternatives? (6) How do we measure success? A feature must pass all gates before development begins.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'co-pilot' and 'autopilot' AI features?
options: Co-pilot is open-source; autopilot is proprietary
Co-pilot assists humans who make final decisions; autopilot acts autonomously
Co-pilot runs locally; autopilot runs in the cloud
Co-pilot uses small models; autopilot uses large models
questions.explanation: Co-pilot mode assists humans (suggestions, drafts, highlights) while humans retain decision authority. Autopilot mode acts autonomously (auto-classification, auto-routing). Use co-pilot when failure cost is high; autopilot when tasks are low-risk and high-volume.

questions.question: What is a confidence UX pattern in AI product design?
options: Showing users the model's training accuracy percentage
Adapting the UI flow based on the model's confidence level — showing disclaimers for low confidence, acting directly for high confidence
A loading animation that shows model processing stages
A user survey that measures trust in AI features
questions.explanation: Confidence UX adapts the interface based on prediction confidence: high confidence (>0.9) → act directly; medium (0.7-0.9) → show with disclaimer; low (<0.7) → flag for human review. This builds user trust and prevents bad outputs from reaching users unchecked.

questions.question: What is an AI Feature Spec?
options: A technical specification for the model architecture
A required document covering problem, solution, failure modes, evaluation plan, and launch criteria before any AI feature ships
An API specification for LLM endpoints
A dataset specification for training data
questions.explanation: An AI Feature Spec is a pre-development document that defines the problem, proposed solution, data requirements, expected failure modes and mitigations, evaluation metrics, and launch criteria. No AI feature should ship without one.

questions.question: Which of these is a common AI product design failure?
options: Using too many evaluation metrics
Shipping an AI feature that works technically but erodes user trust because there's no transparency about when it might be wrong
Using too small a model for the task
Having too many human-in-the-loop checkpoints
questions.explanation: Technical capability without product judgment yields features no one trusts. Users need transparency (how confident is this?), controllability (can I override it?), and predictability (will it behave consistently?). Missing these leads to low adoption regardless of model quality.
